intro.text: Built from the [Technical Design Spec (TDS) — Template](https://app.notion.com/p/406128b264948158a47ffc6690c30962). This is the worked example for other projects. Behaviour is defined in [User Stories](https://app.notion.com/p/405128b2649480a1951cf018caeb9def); this document defines how it's built.

blocks.text: Partner Packs let a client organisation buy a block of points that its employees spend on Scentia short courses. Today there's no self-service: employees find a course in the public catalogue and email Scentia to book, coordinators enrol them by hand, and premium and qualification pack reports are built by combining Salesforce and Moodle CSV exports for each client. Support queries land in the public programs queue or with account managers.

The portal gives employees self-service booking within their contract, gives client administrators approvals, employee lists, usage reporting and renewals, and gives Scentia's two PP coordinators one view across all clients. Salesforce remains the system of record for clients, contracts, courses, offerings and enrolments.

Employees book eligible courses without emailing Scentia.
Client administrators see usage and progress at any time, replacing the manually prepared client reports.
Clients can renew online or request an invoice without contacting their sales rep.
Replacing Salesforce or Moodle as systems of record.
Single sign-on (all users sign in with an email link and code).
Public B2C course purchasing.
Contract emails (renewal reminders, invoices, receipts): Salesforce sends these.

items: **Places and points are rechecked atomically** on submit, approve and change, while Salesforce also sells places through other channels (Book, Approve, Change stories).
**Contract selection rule**: whitelist contract first, then the contract that ends soonest, falling through on insufficient points or out-of-term dates (stories 3.5 AC 2, 4.2 AC 13).
**10-business-day rule** decides whether points are returned or consumed, and whether changes are allowed.

**Holds and auto-expiry**: a pending request holds a place and its points (shown as "pending") for one month, until 10 business days before the start, or until the contract ends, whichever is soonest; reminders at 3 days, end of week, then weekly.
**Approve from email without signing in**, with single-use, expiring, request-bound links.
**Immutable points ledger and activity history**.
**Strict tenant isolation**: admins see only their organisation; internal users see all, view-only for bookings.

**Hourly refresh, live availability**: Salesforce data is refreshed every hour on the hour and the portal shows no freshness timestamps. Availability can't be batch processed, so places remaining are read live from Salesforce at submit, approve and change (stories §2).
**Large exports run in the background** and are delivered when ready.
**Salesforce API budget** is already about 50% used daily (Salesforce Queries meeting).

rows: Same; course list < 500 ms with 500 courses

items: Scentia stack (section 4); Cloudflare team account.
Personal information at rest in Australia.
No SSO; email link and code for all users.

Salesforce is the system of record for clients, contracts, courses, offerings, enrolments and renewal status. Salesforce's data model allows only one-to-one relationships for client admins, so client admins beyond the primary live in the portal.
Salesforce daily API limit is shared with other integrations and already about half used.
Informatica is being replaced by MuleSoft during or after this build.
Project timeline 01/10/2026 – 31/12/2026.
A full-copy Salesforce sandbox with anonymised data is available for staging (confirmed).
An integration user and External Client App can be created at no licence cost (Salesforce Queries meeting).
The integration user can read an offering's live places remaining through the REST API, and run SOQL delta queries on SystemModstamp for each mirrored object.
Qualification progress is available in Salesforce (Q6).

blocks.text: As per the template scheme.

items: Every tenant-owned table carries organisation_id (denormalised onto booking, ledger and audit for direct filtering).
Client admin and participant requests run with a tenant context derived from the session; repositories refuse queries without one.
Postgres row-level security keyed on a per-transaction setting is the second line of defence.
Internal routes use an explicit cross-tenant context, and booking mutations are not exposed to internal roles (view-only, per stories).
Integration tests attempt cross-tenant reads and writes for every admin route.

blocks.text: Drizzle migrations, expand-and-contract, reviewed in PR, run by CI.

A nightly job purges expired tokens, sessions and export files. A yearly job de-identifies personal information older than its retention period: names and emails are replaced with a stable pseudonym, so the ledger and audit stay intact.

rows: OAuth 2.0 client credentials via an External Client App and a dedicated integration user per environment, least-privilege permission set

Hourly sync every hour on the hour (Cron Trigger): a SOQL delta query on SystemModstamp since the last cursor for each mirrored object (Account, contract, contract course, course, offering, enrolment, renewal), upserted into the mirror, with side effects such as notifying bookings of a cancelled or rescheduled offering. Places remaining are read live for the offering at submit, approve and change, because availability can't be batch processed. No data-freshness timestamps are shown in the portal (stories §2, ADR-003)
Queued writes using Composite API upserts on external ID Portal_Booking_Id__c / Portal_Renewal_Id__c, making retries idempotent
Booking confirmed, changed, cancelled (with points returned or consumed); employee removed; renewal invoice requested; online renewal paid; bank transfer chosen (with payment reference)
Accounts, contracts, contract courses, courses, offerings with places remaining, offering changes, enrolments and progress, renewal status, renewal pricing, primary admin contact

Estimated < 2,000 calls/day at design scale: about 170 for hourly deltas (24 × 7 objects), up to about 1,200 live place checks at the peak booking rate, plus writes. Daily API usage is monitored and alerts at 80% of the share agreed with the SF admin (Q8). Composite API batches up to 25 subrequests
Exponential backoff (max 8 attempts over ~24 h), then DLQ. Failed bookings shown to internal users as problems ("Problems are flagged") and resolvable by retry or cancel
Nightly SOQL delta query on SystemModstamp since the last run for each mirrored object, plus a points comparison (SF used vs ledger) per active contract, with drift reported in the internal portal
Salesforce org location TBC; out of portal scope
When MuleSoft replaces Informatica, only the Salesforce client in src/server changes; the portal uses standard REST and SOQL
API key; webhooks verified with Svix signatures

Sign-in emails are sent inline (latency matters); all others go through the email queue

Queue retries; bounces and complaints add the address to a suppression list and flag the user to admins

blocks.text: Server functions per route group, validated with Zod. External endpoints: POST /webhooks/stripe, POST /webhooks/resend, GET+POST /a/:token (action links), GET+POST /unsubscribe/:token.

items: Submit, approve and change run in one Postgres transaction that locks the offering row and the candidate contract rows (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), recomputes places and points, and writes the booking, ledger entry and outbox rows together (transactional outbox).

Places available = Salesforce places remaining, read live for the offering at submit, approve and change − portal holds and confirmations not yet acknowledged by Salesforce. If Salesforce can't be reached, the mirrored count is used.
Pending requests hold a place and their points ("pending"); places and points are rechecked on approval (stories 3.5 AC 7–8, 4.7).
Salesforce can still sell the last place through other channels. A Salesforce rejection triggers compensation (booking failed, points returned, participant and coordinators told). See R1 and Q2.

blocks.text: As per the standard.

Offerings store UTC plus the venue's IANA timezone; displayed in the venue timezone for in-person and in the viewer's time zone for online (detected from the browser and stored on the user, so emails and calendar invites use it too). The zone label is always shown (story 3.4 AC 4). Business days use the calendar in Q3.

Better Auth email OTP (6 digits) and magic link in one email, valid 10 minutes, single use, stored hashed. Limits: 5 code requests per email per hour, 5 wrong attempts per code, IP rate limits, Turnstile on the email form. Clicking the magic link signs the user in (story 3.1 AC 4): the page it opens submits a POST automatically, with a button if scripts are off, so scanners that only fetch the URL can't consume it. Messages follow story 3.1: a matching domain not on a restricted list is told it has no access; unrecognised domains and clients that aren't live yet get one "not recognised" message that reveals no clients. The break-glass account (story 5.3) doesn't use email sign-in: long password plus passkey or authenticator app (Better Auth plugins, Q16).
One session per user; elevated access is time-boxed by when the user last verified.

rows: Re-verify to reach /admin after 24 h; participant pages still work
Story 5.3; every sign-in alerts IT and the list owner

blocks.text: Role and list membership are read from the database on every request, so demotion or removal applies on the next page load. Removing a super admin revokes their sessions.
See Appendix C for the full matrix. Checks are in src/server guards per route group plus per-record tenant checks.

Approve, decline and unsubscribe links carry a random 256-bit token stored hashed, bound to one record and purpose, single use, expiring after 7 days or when the request closes (whichever is first). Approve completes on opening the link and shows the result (story 4.7): the page submits a POST automatically, with a button if scripts are off. Decline opens a page for an optional reason before confirming. Unsubscribe applies straight away (story 3.9), and mail clients can use RFC 8058 one-click. Expired or used links go to sign-in; a request another admin already decided shows its current status.

As per standard. Salesforce integration user can't sign in interactively. The break-glass account can do everything a super admin can, including managing the super admin list, but can't change the list owner or sign in to the client or participant portals; its actions are labelled break-glass in the audit log.
